source_spans.locator: Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 32(1), published p.3, Abstract: human subjects commit internal allocation to a nonfixated visual position; the trajectory is inferred from momentary changes in detection efficiency

Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 32(1), published pp.4-5, definitions and measurement logic: internal alignment is distinguished from detecting; internal spatial allocation is manipulated by instruction/probability and measured through changes in detection efficiency

Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 32(1), published pp.6-8, central predictive-cue experiments: maintained fixation/EOG control, neutral plus versus directional arrows, 0.8 valid/0.2 invalid target probability, and reaction-time benefits/costs across simple and choice tasks

Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 32(1), published pp.10-12, separate analogue-movement experiments: arrow instruction to a far peripheral target, variable cue-probe SOA, target/intermediate/opposite probe positions, and maximum relative intermediate-position advantage at about 150 ms; analogue interpretation stated as provisional

Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 32(1), published pp.21-22, Conclusions: time-locked covert shifts are measurable through converging efficiency measures; criterion-shift language is acknowledged as an alternative description but constrained by the observed pattern

conditions: central fixation is maintained while a neutral plus cue or central directional cue sets the probability of a later luminance target on the left or right

in a separate trajectory experiment, a central arrow instructs internal allocation toward a visible far peripheral target while low-probability probes may appear at the target, intermediate, or opposite positions
population: normal human participants in the psychophysical experiments reviewed by the source
task: simple or choice reaction-time detection under neutral, valid, and invalid central-cue conditions
detect low-probability probes presented at different spatial positions and stimulus-onset asynchronies after an instruction to allocate toward a far peripheral target
temporal_scope: the central predictive-cue cost/benefit experiments and the separate variable-SOA trajectory experiments are distinct procedures; in the latter, the greatest relative intermediate-position advantage occurred at about 150 ms

nodes.description: central neutral or directional cue that changes the probability distribution over the later target position while fixation is maintained
whether the target occurs at the directionally indicated position, at the opposite position, or under a neutral non-directional cue
internal alignment with a source position in visual space without requiring an eye movement
arbitrary assigned manual or verbal response indicating that the visual event has been detected
latency of the assigned response to the detected visual event
neutral/valid/invalid central-cue reaction-time procedure used to compare detection efficiency while eye position is held fixed
central arrow instructing internal allocation toward a visible peripheral target in the separate trajectory experiment
location of the low-probability detection probe relative to the instructed far target, including target, intermediate, and opposite-side positions
stimulus-onset interval between the movement instruction and the later detection probe in the trajectory experiment
source-proposed analogue trajectory whose position-dependent detection advantage changes over time after the instruction
variable-SOA multi-position detection procedure used to test whether the internal spatial shift can be time-locked and whether intermediate positions receive transient advantage
the stimulus has reached a processing level at which an arbitrary experimenter-assigned report response can be made

relations.description: in the central predictive-cue experiments, response latency is shorter with valid spatial information and longer with invalid information relative to the neutral condition
the neutral/valid/invalid procedure uses reaction-time differences as the observable measure of cue-dependent detection efficiency
the source interprets the cue-dependent performance differences under maintained fixation as a change in internal spatial alignment
in the separate trajectory experiment, reaction time varies jointly with probe position and elapsed interval after the instruction

the source treats the position-by-time reaction-time pattern, including the greatest relative intermediate-position advantage at about 150 ms, as provisional support for a time-locked analogue trajectory
changes in internal spatial alignment are operationally measured through changes in the efficiency and latency of detecting events at different positions
an assigned report response is the operational indication that the event has reached the source-defined detection level
